source_observations.title: Our Rules
source_observations.scope: Complete 125-line public body read; no effective date visible. Apps/software require original creative thinking, an existing category and a demonstrated prototype. AI use requires human creativity, involvement and transparency; little or no human thought/involvement is prohibited. Submitted materials require rights. External engagement funneling and service-provider-centered projects are prohibited. Enforcement may restrict accounts/projects. Charity allowance is independently detailed in K04.

source_observations.title: Who can use Kickstarter?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Creators must be adults. Individuals need residence and government ID matching the launch country, with an EU-ID exception. Entities launch where registered through an authorized owner/executive; beneficial owners and requested directors undergo verification. ID/tax documents, an appropriately named supported bank account and named card are required. A euro/IBAN exception permits specified cross-border accounts without replacing eligible-country/address verification; Canadian projects require credit cards.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Can Kickstarter be used to fund anything?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. A project must create something new with a clear endpoint and credible completion path. An already available product cannot itself be the campaign endpoint. Investment returns and monetary rewards are prohibited; project approval remains Kickstarter's decision.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Can business and nonprofit entities raise funds for projects?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Businesses and nonprofits can qualify. Nonprofits must fund a specific new, shareable endeavor, not general mission support. Up to 10% of campaign funds may go to charity if disclosed on submission; reward items may also be donated. A recipient need not be a registered nonprofit, but the donation must relate to the project and avoid personal fundraising. Pledges are generally not tax-deductible; possible project-specific exceptions do not establish PYA tax status.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Fees: United States
source_observations.scope: Complete current public US fee table read. Successful US campaigns incur a 5% platform fee plus processing of 3% and $0.30 per pledge. Pledges under $10 use processing of 5% and $0.08. Unfunded campaigns incur no platform/processing fees. This US table is not a global applicant quote.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Kickstarter Fees: A Comprehensive Guide for Creators
source_observations.scope: Complete 64-line public blog body read. The older guide states a $0.05 micropledge fixed component, conflicting with K05's current $0.08. It also identifies fulfillment, staff, shipping, rewards, marketing and tax costs beyond platform fees.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: How to set the right funding goal for your Kickstarter campaign
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Funding is all-or-nothing: an unmet goal yields no collected pledges or creator funds. The goal should cover completion, rewards, fees and relevant taxes; goal/deadline cannot change after launch. Budget planning should use actual resource estimates. The documented calculator accepts a budget and tax assumption; no project estimate or calculator was entered.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: What is the maximum project duration?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Campaigns run 1–60 days. Kickstarter recommends 30 days or less. The funding duration/deadline cannot be adjusted after launch.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: If my project is successfully funded, how do I receive my funds?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. For the ordinary successful campaign, collection/processing lasts 14 calendar days after the deadline, then a single payout is initiated to one account. Bank availability may take another 3–14 business days. This is not a guaranteed availability date; installment and Late Pledge routes have separate schedules.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Pledge Over Time FAQ
source_observations.scope: Relevant published sections through lines 82 read, including current/legacy payout distinction; no checkout or feature enabled. Optional installments split qualifying pledges into three charges. For first payouts on/after January 15, 2026, the first payment arrives around the ordinary payout, followed by approximately eight- and twelve-week payouts. The feature has no extra fee according to this Help page. Failed subsequent collections can drop pledges; it is not immediately available maintenance cash.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: How will I be paid out for Late Pledges?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Optional Late Pledge payouts start seven days after the ordinary campaign payout, then recur weekly while applicable. Unsettled or sub-threshold amounts can delay/bundle payouts; the original campaign bank account is used. This feature was not enabled.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: What is a creator obligated to do once their project is funded?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. The Help page assigns creators responsibility for promised work and rewards, honest responses and regular progress/delay updates. If fulfillment becomes impossible, creators must make reasonable efforts toward another satisfactory conclusion. It links current Terms section 4 and distinguishes projects launched before February 11, 2025; the linked full legal body was not verified.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: If I am unable to complete my project as promised, what should I do?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Creator failure guidance calls for reasonable resolution efforts including refund offers, communication and an update accounting for completed work, use of funds and obstacles. If inability to perform is known before funding ends, the creator is expected to cancel.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Does Kickstarter issue refunds?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Kickstarter describes itself as neither a store nor the party issuing creator refunds. Backers request collected-pledge refunds from the creator; exhausted production funds may prevent them. Creator-issued refunds may take up to 30 days to reach the original payment method. These Help statements do not establish an unconditional legal no-refund entitlement.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: How do I issue a refund to one of my backers?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Creators can issue full or partial refunds through the backer report. Before campaign payout, platform and processing fees are returned; after payout the creator bears those fees. Refunds use a saved/new creator card. Active payment disputes and invalid original payment methods can require separate handling. No refund workflow was used.
source_observations.research_lane: In-session peer primary research; author read the complete handed-off findings and independently checked decisive Rules, fit, nonprofit and fee sources.

source_observations.title: Can I use AI-generated content or create AI technology in my project?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. AI-generated output requires disclosure of tools, incorporation, original work and AI-created elements. AI technology projects must identify data sources and explain consent/credit safeguards; lacking consent processes makes admission unlikely. Approved responses appear publicly. No finding about PYA training data, human contribution or admissibility was made.

source_observations.title: How can I access my expired backer report?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Automatic report/PII access expires two years from the latest estimated reward delivery date; renewed access requires a reviewed request. Guidance restricts reuse to fulfillment, limits collaborator sharing, prohibits shared-computer access, and calls for deleting the downloaded file after all rewards are delivered.

source_observations.title: How long does a project remain on Kickstarter?
source_observations.scope: Public article body read through web retrieval; no account interaction. Project records persist after failure/cancellation; account deletion does not erase launched pages, updates or comments. Support may consider hiding a project. Unsubmitted drafts can be deleted; submitted drafts cannot simply be deleted.

source_observations.title: How can I cancel my project?
